title: Unsegregated audiences in Minneapolis
summary: Phillips says Minneapolis audiences were not segregated, were mostly Black, and the pianist's and drummer's wives were white.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What kind of audiences would you play for? Did they segregate the audiences?
No. Not in Minneapolis. Minneapolis wasn't segregated.
Did they have a lot of Black people that would come and listen?
Sure. More black than was white. Oh yeah,
sure. The piano player, his wife was white, and so was the drummer's wife.
